detail.abstract:
Background: Tactical Combat Casualty Care for All Service Members (TCCC-ASM) aims to prepare military personnel to provide self-aid and buddy aid in combat. However, the extent to which acquired competencies are retained and translated into effective action during real combat remains poorly understood. This study evaluated the influence of first combat experience on the practical application of TCCC-ASM among mobilized military personnel during the Russo-Ukrainian War. 

Methods: A multicohort observational study with a mixed retrospective-prospective design was conducted between August 2022 and May 2026. Data from five independent cohorts were integrated, including educational assessments, structured surveys, operational observations, prehospital medical documentation, medical evacuation records, and rehabilitation data. The primary endpoint was the actual implementation of TCCC-ASM knowledge and skills during first combat experience. Transfer of training into operational practice was quantified using the authors' Training-to-Performance Index (TP-index). 

Results: A total of 1,961 participants were included. Although all participants successfully completed TCCC-ASM training, only 539 of 1,082 service members with combat experience (49.8%) subsequently encountered situations requiring the practical application of TCCC-ASM knowledge and skills. Among 327 wounded personnel, self-aid was performed by 71 individuals (21.7%), whereas 78.3% required buddy aid. The TP-index for self-aid was 0.132 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.104-0.163), indicating a substantial gap between successful training completion and performance under real combat conditions. Major barriers included severe pain, inability to recall procedures, panic reactions, limited visibility, and delayed evacuation. First combat experience was also associated with reassessment of the practical relevance of training and a unanimous demand for refresher training. A preprint-June 27, 2026 

Conclusions: A measurable gap exists between successful completion of TCCC-ASM training and the practical implementation of acquired competencies during combat. This phenomenon, defined as the Training-to-Performance Gap, highlights the limitations of relying solely on educational outcomes when evaluating military medical training. The proposed TP-index provides a quantitative framework for assessing the transfer of training into operational performance and supports the implementation of structured refresher training following first combat experience.

title: Queen Bee Reproductive Personalization: How Delegation Failure, Black-Boxed Knowledge, and Symbolic Nesting Undermine Succession Development
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Queen Bee Reproductive Personalization: How Delegation Failure, Black-Boxed Knowledge, and Symbolic Nesting Undermine Succession Development
detail.abstract:
This paper reconceptualizes personalization in organizations not merely as the concentration of task knowledge or authority, but as the concentration of an organization’s reproductive functions in a symbolically central individual. In this paper, reproduction does not refer to biological reproduction. Rather, it refers to the organizational process through which skills, judgment criteria, responsibility, evaluative standards, and workplace culture are transmitted to future members. While personalization has often been discussed as a problem of insufficient documentation, poor handover, or operational continuity risk, this paper focuses on a deeper problem: the condition in which not only current work, but also the capacity to develop successors, becomes dependent on a single person.

This paper calls this structure Queen Bee Reproductive Personalization. In eusocial insects, the concentration of reproductive function in the queen operates as an adaptive division of labor for colony survival. In human organizations, however, the concentration of succession development, knowledge transfer, delegation, responsibility transfer, evaluative judgment, and cultural continuity in one symbolically central individual may become organizationally pathological. Human organizations do not survive because one individual continues to “produce the future”; they survive because knowledge, judgment, responsibility, and culture are distributed, shared, questioned, and renewed across members.

The paper argues that Queen Bee Reproductive Personalization develops through a self-reinforcing process involving competence, responsibility, symbolic capital, delegation failure, micromanagement, reduced psychological safety, organizational silence, and the black-boxing of knowledge. A competent and responsible central figure may initially support the organization. However, when that person’s competence is not transformed into shared knowledge, transferable responsibility, the development of successors, and a renewable culture, the organization becomes increasingly dependent on that individual. As subordinates lose opportunities to judge, fail, ask questions, and assume responsibility, they may become workers who follow instructions rather than successors who can reproduce the organization’s knowledge and judgment.
The paper further argues that personalization appears not only in knowledge and decision-making, but also in workplace space. When a particular person’s objects, awards, dedicated tools, visual traces, spatial arrangements, and work routines accumulate in a shared workplace, the space itself may become a symbolic nest that preserves that person’s memory and authority. This paper calls this process Symbolic Nesting. It also introduces the concept of the Residual Queen Effect, referring to the persistence of a queen bee-type individual’s influence through objects, spatial arrangements, organizational memory, silence, and routines even after that person is no longer physically central to the workplace.

This paper extends the prior Queen Bee Structure framework. Whereas the previous Queen Bee Structure paper examined how an established queen bee structure becomes culturally reproduced through Worker Bee Zombies, this paper moves one step backward and asks how such a structure emerges in the first place. It examines why a workplace becomes unable to reproduce knowledge, judgment, responsibility, and culture without a queen bee-type individual. The paper also connects this framework to Structural Selection Pressure, Silent Harassment, and Ma-Meme. Ma-Meme, an abbreviation of Multiple Anger Meme, is treated here as a secondary framework for understanding how anger-based behaviors may later become culturally reproduced through psychological reward, organizational justification, and social imitation.

The central claim of this paper is that the real danger for organizations is not the presence of a strong individual. The danger emerges when that strength does not produce successors. Queen Bee Reproductive Personalization describes a structure in which an organization appears to be supported by competence, while failing to become competent itself.

detail.title: The Learning Power of Firms: A New Dimension of Competitive Advantage in the Age of AI

publicationDetails.journalName: INSEAD Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: The organizational learning literature has long recognized the strategic value of learning, but has conceptualized it primarily as a human-centered, episodic, and reflective capability. The proliferation of artificial intelligence fundamentally alters these assumptions: learning is increasingly embedded in operational systems, continuous in tempo, and distributed across the full surface of organizational activity rather than concentrated in designated learning units. This paper introduces the concept of learning power-a composite organizational capability constituted by four interdependent dimensions: learning density (the proportion of organizational interactions that generate usable insight), learning velocity (the speed with which insight is translated into changed system behavior), learning scale (the number of simultaneous learning processes the organization can sustain), and learning directionality (the alignment of learning objectives with strategic intent and organizational values). We propose that competitive advantage in AI-enabled environments is increasingly determined by the multiplicative combination of these four dimensions-Learning Power = Density × Velocity × Scale × Directionalityrather than by any single component. We further distinguish the concept of the learning surface-the distributed organizational architecture through which AI-enabled learning operates-from the learning units and episodic learning processes that characterize conventional accounts. The paper situates the learning power framework within the context of companion contributions on AI competitive architecture (Dutta & Doz, INSEAD Working Paper, 2026/38/STR), programmable strategy (Doz & Dutta, INSEAD Working Paper, 2026/39/STR), and strategic envelope governance (Dutta & Doz, INSEAD Working Paper, 2026/40/STR), and draws out implications for organizational learning theory, dynamic capabilities, and the human governance of machine learning systems.

title: The Softmax of Default: Exact Pricing and Analytic Risk Attribution for First-to-Default Basket Swaps with Heterogeneous Recoveries
affiliations: ZHAW School of Management and Law

detail.title: The Softmax of Default: Exact Pricing and Analytic Risk Attribution for First-to-Default Basket Swaps with Heterogeneous Recoveries
detail.abstract: First-to-default (FtD) basket swaps pay the loss of whichever name defaults first. With heterogeneous recoveries the payo! depends on the first defaulter's identity, so name-level allocation and stable Greeks are typically delegated to generic basket engines. This letter shows that under a common-baseline separable-exponential survival structure, the first-defaulter identity is exactly independent of the first-default time, with deterministic Boltzmann-Gibbs (softmax) weights. The identity calculus extends beyond independence: exact separation persists, with the same weights, under common multiplicative frailty, and survives with shock-driven weights under Marshall-Olkin common shocks once a tie rule is specified. Under copula dependence the constant softmax generally becomes time-varying, while pricing remains one-dimensional. The FtD protection value then factorizes into a severity term (the expected LGD of the first defaulter) and a timing term (the value of a unit first-default claim), delivering simulation-free pricing, deterministic name-level attribution, and analytic Greeks under standard CDS conventions. A public-data illustration supplies a diagnostic for the common-baseline restriction and checks the analytic spread against Monte Carlo under the same calibrated model; for the studied basket, the fit is tight across calm and stress regimes. Further extensions (heterogeneous baselines, piecewiseexact tenor-grid calibration, and stochastic recoveries) and detailed proofs are in an Online Appendix.

title: From AI Literacy to AI Fluency: A Developmental Framework for Higher Education

detail.title: From AI Literacy to AI Fluency: A Developmental Framework for Higher Education

declarations.ethicsApproval: There were no human subjects included in this study

detail.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence has moved rapidly into teaching, learning, research, and administrative work, yet the dominant institutional response has centered on AI literacy alone. This conceptual article argues that AI literacy, defined as understanding basic concepts, recognizing tools, performing basic tasks, and identifying broad risks such as bias, hallucination, privacy harm, and misinformation, is necessary but insufficient for higher education in the generative era. The article advances a developmental AI Fluency framework that extends literacy toward strategic, critical, ethical, and contextual use of artificial intelligence while preserving human judgment, authorship, accountability, and disciplinary standards. The framework specifies six developmental levels, from AI Exposure and AI Awareness through Functional and Critical AI Literacy and on to Disciplinary AI Fluency, Generative AI Fluency, and Responsible AI Leadership, with the lower tiers forming a literacy band and the higher tiers forming a fluency band. It pairs these levels with six competency domains spanning conceptual understanding, operational skill, epistemic verification, ethical and legal judgment, metacognitive and human agency, and disciplinary transfer. A central claim is that fluency is a socio-technical capacity rather than an individual skill alone, depending on curriculum design, assessment redesign, faculty development, equitable access, policy, data governance, and human-centered principles. The article concludes that institutions should treat AI fluency as a core learning outcome and offers implications for practice and a research agenda.

detail.abstract: The shift from prompt engineering to agentic, multi-agent large language model (LLM) systems has moved the locus of value from the design of individual instructions to the coordination of systems in which models plan, invoke tools, retrieve context, and collaborate across specialized roles (Wang et al., 2024; Xi et al., 2023; Guo et al., 2024). This transition introduces a class of goal-directed, partially autonomous systems whose growing capability is accompanied by hallucination and reliability concerns (Zhao et al., 2026), adversarial exposure through tool access (OWASP Foundation, 2025), and coordination-driven scaling complexity (Guo et al., 2024). The paper argue that prompt engineering alone is insufficient for these conditions: optimizing a single instruction does not determine how tasks are routed and sequenced, how tool access is bounded, how outputs are validated, or how institutions remain accountable for autonomous action problems that are inherently socio-technical (National Institute of Standards and Technology, 2023). This article's contribution is the AI Memetic Orchestration Framework (AMOF), a proposed six-layer conceptual model comprising Memetic, Boundary, Framework, Orchestration, Evaluation, and Governance layers, that integrates currently fragmented work on agent design patterns (Anthropic, 2024), guardrails and oversight (OpenAI, 2025; Verdiesen et al., 2020; Sterz et al., 2024), and risk-management standards (National Institute of Standards and Technology, 2023; Microsoft Corporation, 2022) into a coherent scaffold for designing and governing orchestrated LLM systems. The paper position AMOF beyond prompt engineering, context engineering, workflow automation, and software architecture; introduce AI memetics, boundary prompting, and framework engineering as explicitly proposed rather than established constructs; and frame the responsible operation of agentic AI as the deliberate, layered orchestration of memetic, bounded, frameworkdriven, evaluated, and governed components that balance autonomous capability against bounded human oversight.

detail.abstract:
This paper develops a formal theoretical model of decision-making under internal conflict, conceptualized as conflict-penalized selection among heterogeneous behavioral and organizational layers. Unlike preference-based, dual-process, or bounded rationality approaches, the model treats inconsistency not as preference instability or cognitive error, but as the outcome of time-varying dominance among distinct functional components: Identification (authorship and feasibility), Relational and Institutional Constraint (social and governance pressures), Influence Persistence (habit and routine dynamics), and Justificatory Constraint (beliefs and permissibility conditions).

The model is structured as a two-stage process separating internal selection from external expression, where selection determines the chosen action through a conflict-penalized score and expression governs how that action becomes observable through timing, communication, and implementation conditions. This separation allows coherent internal decisions to be analytically distinguished from failures in signaling, rollout, or reception.

The paper introduces Lifestyle Coherence as a trajectory-level construct evaluating whether repeated sequences of selection, expression, and feedback preserve authorship, structural alignment, and conflict absorption over time. The framework generates testable implications for phenomena such as procrastination, compliance without agreement, preference reversals, organizational rollout failure, and performative agreement.

By integrating layered conflict mechanisms, expressive transformation, and dynamic feedback into a unified formulation, the model provides a diagnostic alternative to standard decision-theoretic accounts and offers a basis for empirical analysis of behavioral and organizational inconsistency across repeated decision cycles.

title: Governance Concentration in Decentralized Finance: A Comparative Analysis of MakerDAO, Lido, and Ethereum Name Service Using the Zero Point Senemosìa Framework

detail.title: Governance Concentration in Decentralized Finance: A Comparative Analysis of MakerDAO, Lido, and Ethereum Name Service Using the Zero Point Senemosìa Framework
detail.abstract: Decentralized Autonomous Organizations (DAOs) promise democratic governance through token-weighted voting, yet empirical evidence reveals extreme concentration of voting power comparable to the world's most unequal countries. This paper introduces the Zero Point Senemosìa (ZPS) framework, a novel approach to quantifying governance health in DAOs through quantum-inspired organizational modeling. We analyze three major DAOs-MakerDAO (MKR), Lido (LDO), and Ethereum Name Service (ENS)-revealing distinct governance pathologies: MKR exhibits polarized debate (DHI = 0.68), LDO demonstrates silent consensus masking concentration (DHI = 0.71), and ENS presents acute treasury capture risk despite high participation (DHI = 0.59). Our analysis reveals Gini coefficients ranging from 0.80-0.89 and Nakamoto coefficients as low as 4, indicating that merely 4-7 entities control 51% of governance in these protocols worth $14B+ in total value locked. We introduce the DAO Health Index (DHI) as a quantitative governance metric and propose the Protocol for Auto-corrective Reconfiguration and Equilibrium (PARE) as a framework for designing self-correcting governance mechanisms. Our findings have direct implications for regulatory policy, institutional investment, and the design of future decentralized systems.

detail.abstract: Urban parks are nominally public goods, yet access to green space is deeply unequal across neighborhoods. This paper constructs a novel Park Accessibility Index for all 2,167 census tracts in New York City that augments boundary-based park coverage with buffer-zone green space at 0.1 and 0.2 miles, reducing the fraction of tracts classified as entirely park-inaccessible from 50 to 21 percent. Using SafeGraph mobility data from 2018 to 2022, we exploit the COVID-19 pandemic as a quasi-natural experiment to estimate how park access mediates the behavioral and welfare consequences of a large mobility shock. In a matched difference-indifferences design, park-deprived tracts experienced approximately 47 fewer park visitors per month and a 7 percent decline in log visits relative to matched park-rich tracts. Applying the travel cost method, we estimate that park-deprived tracts lost 42.7 percent of their annual park consumer surplus post-COVID, compared to 30.2 percent for park-rich tracts-a 41 percent larger proportional welfare loss. The disparity is sharpest for low-income households within park-deprived communities, who lost over half their baseline park welfare. Our findings document a welfare externality of chronic park underfunding that standard fiscal analysis omits.

title: Hedges of the Digital Age: A VAR-GARCH Analysis of Gold, Cryptocurrency, and Geopolitical Leading Indicators (2016-2026)

detail.title: Hedges of the Digital Age: A VAR-GARCH Analysis of Gold, Cryptocurrency, and Geopolitical Leading Indicators (2016-2026)
detail.abstract: This study examines whether gold (GLD) and Bitcoin (BTC-USD) respond differently to geopolitical stress signals, using daily data spanning January 2016 to February 2026. Employing VAR-GARCH and IGARCH specifications alongside Granger causality tests and Chow structural break analysis, we investigate the safe-haven properties of both assets under geopolitical risk, with particular attention to U.S. tariff escalations between January 2025 and February 2026. A confirmed structural break on April 2, 2025 demarcates full-sample and sub-period analyses. Within the Liberation Day window, the iShares U.S. Aerospace and Defence ETF (ITA) Granger-precedes BTC-USD (p=0.013) and shows borderline predictive content for GLD (p=0.091), suggesting that defence equity markets transmit geopolitical stress signals to both assets. BTC-USD exhibits Integrated GARCH behaviour (α+β = 1.000), implying permanent volatility persistence, while GLD's α+β = 0.988 gives a volatility half-life of approximately 57 trading days, indicating mean reversion. During acute geopolitical stress, GLD functions as a safe haven while BTC-USD is abandoned, underscoring their structurally divergent roles in the global monetary system.

detail.abstract:
Who gets counted determines who gets care. Public health funding and policy decisions rely on data systems that routinely underrepresent people experiencing homelessness, undocumented immigrants, non-English speakers, rural residents, and other underserved populations. At the same time, the termination of 444 Centers for Disease Control and Prevention grants totaling $5.78 billion has raised significant questions about the future of the nation’s public health infrastructure.

This policy brief examines the intersection of federal public health funding reductions, legal challenges, and structural data exclusion. Drawing on Congressional Research Service reports, federal court filings, agency documents, and peer-reviewed research, it distinguishes verified facts from policy analysis while assessing the consequences for health equity and community-based public health practice.

The paper also introduces the She Is Us United Community Data Framework, an operational model that uses Community Health Workers, trauma-informed engagement, and longitudinal data collection to reach populations often excluded from traditional surveillance. It argues that strengthening community-generated data can improve Community Health Needs Assessments, support evidence-based policymaking, and produce a more accurate understanding of health needs. The findings suggest that restoring public health infrastructure requires not only renewed investment but also new approaches to ensuring every community is counted.

detail.abstract: The tumor microenvironment (TME) is a dynamic and complex ecosystem composed of malignant cells and surrounding stromal, immune, vascular, and extracellular matrix components that collectively influence cancer development and therapeutic outcomes. Major constituents of the TME include cancer-associated fibroblasts, tumor-associated macrophages, lymphocytes, endothelial cells, cytokines, chemokines, and extracellular matrix proteins. Increasing evidence demonstrates that these cellular and non-cellular elements actively regulate tumor initiation, progression, and metastatic dissemination by promoting cancer cell proliferation, angiogenesis, invasion, and immune evasion. The TME also contributes significantly to therapeutic resistance by establishing immunosuppressive conditions that impair antitumor immune responses and reduce the efficacy of conventional therapies and immune checkpoint inhibitors. Interactions between tumor cells and the surrounding microenvironment facilitate the recruitment of suppressive immune cells, remodeling of the extracellular matrix, and secretion of protumorigenic mediators that support tumor survival and metastatic colonization. Recent advances in cancer biology have highlighted the therapeutic potential of targeting the TME through strategies such as immune checkpoint blockade, reprogramming of tumorassociated macrophages, inhibition of angiogenesis, and modulation of stromal signaling pathways. These approaches aim to transform the immunosuppressive microenvironment into one that supports effective antitumor immunity and enhances treatment responsiveness. A comprehensive understanding of the molecular and cellular mechanisms governing the TME offers new opportunities for precision oncology and the development of personalized therapeutic interventions that improve clinical outcomes and the effectiveness of cancer immunotherapy.

detail.abstract: Measuring marketplace activity is essential for understanding informal economies, yet reliable data remain limited because much of this activity occurs outside formal statistical systems. We develop a scalable AI-driven framework that advances existing satellite-based approaches by tracking temporal changes in marketplace footprints, enabling longitudinal measurement of informal market dynamics. Applied to North Korea, where conventional economic data are largely unavailable and direct ground-level data collection is infeasible, the framework produces a nationwide 17-year panel covering 482 marketplaces from 2008 to 2024. We show that marketplace area reflects local economic activity through cross-sectional benchmarks, macro-level responses to economic shocks, and panel regressions at multiple spatial scales. Using this validated measure, we document that marketplace expansion in North Korea was nationwide and decentralized, and that the rank-size distribution of marketplaces follows power-law patterns similar to those observed in other economies. Our findings demonstrate that AI-driven analysis of high-resolution satellite imagery provides a scalable foundation for studying the spatial dynamics of informal economic activity in fragile and data-scarce environments.

title: Entrepreneurial Spillovers from Public R&D: Evidence from the Space Race

detail.title: Entrepreneurial Spillovers from Public R&D: Evidence from the Space Race
detail.abstract: This paper studies how mission-oriented public R&D generates entrepreneurial spillovers. I use the Space Race as a large, technology-specific public R&D shock and the 1979 ERISA reform as an expansion in the supply of venture capital (VC). The Space Race created localized stocks of technical knowledge, specialized human capital, and contractor experience in space-related technologies. After the ERISA reform, VC flowed disproportionately to county-industries that had received NASA funding, and these county-industries experienced higher growth in establishments and employment. Using novel individual-level data on U.S. scientists, I further show that scientists with space-related specialties were more likely to start businesses after the VC supply expansion, especially those employed by NASA prime contractors. The findings show that public R&D spillovers operate not only through patents or incumbent-firm innovation, but also through the formation of new firms. Public R&D can create entrepreneurial potential that remains latent until VC helps in translating scientific capabilities into entrepreneurial outcomes.

detail.abstract: Traditional frameworks for Collaborative Online International Learning (COIL) treat digital tools as passive background infrastructure, inadvertently penalizing Global South institutions due to baseline readiness and preparedness gaps. This policy brief challenges the status quo by operationalizing Techno-Intercultural Synergy Theory (TIST)-a paradigm shifting Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) from a utility to an agentic collaborative partner. Based on rigorous structural equation modeling (R² = .480, Cohen's d = 1.14), this brief demonstrates that AI integration serves a vital dual purpose: minimizing human intercultural friction while independently engineering standalone professional self-efficacy. Actionable macro-level policies are proposed to leverage AI as an equity multiplier, closing the systemic North-South developmental divide without high-carbon physical mobility budgets.

detail.title: US Robot Impacts in Developing Countries: Evidence from Colombian Workers
detail.abstract: This paper examines how robotization in developed countries impacts workers' earnings and labor dynamics in developing countries. Using nearly a decade of Colombian Social Security records and US robot adoption data, we provide robust evidence that workers in industries highly exposed to US robots experience lower cumulative earnings overall and lower employment for older workers and those employed in larger firms. Workers switching firms within the same industry avoid earnings losses, while those moving across industries face the largest losses, consistent with loss of industry-specific human capital. These effects are driven by reduced Colombian exports to the US, particularly in the primary sector, and are more pronounced among older, high-earning workers and those in larger firms, plausibly more integrated into global value chains and, therefore, more directly exposed to foreign automation.

detail.abstract: Traders need a stable, asset-agnostic way to separate ordinary price fluctuation from statistically unusual movement, and the practitioner bands in common use are not calibrated to that question. We study a deliberately simple, causal volatility envelopea band built from the rolling mean and standard deviation of recent returns, anchored on the prior close-and show that it is a stably calibrated classifier of normal versus abnormal next-bar behavior across asset classes, a century of regimes, and daily-tomonthly time scales. That invariance, not the level of any single number, is the finding. On the S&P 500 (1927-2024) the inner (±1σ) band contains the next close 71.20% of the time and stays within 68.7-73.7% in every calendar decade; across a forty-asset universe the mean is 71.9% (cross-asset SD 2.3pp), and the result survives out-of-sample splits, an independently randomized universe, alternative source prices, and weekly and monthly frequencies. Because the band plugs in an estimated μ, σ, the proper null is the finite-window (prediction-t) quantile-67.46% at n = 60, not the known-parameter 68.27%. The +3.7pp excess over that null is the fingerprint of return leptokurtosis rather than an artifact: a GARCH(1,1) with Student-t(ν = 6) innovations reproduces the empirical rate within 0.08pp, and a probability-integral-transform analysis shows the departure from Gaussian is one of shape (heavy tails), not scale. The return-space construction is what carries the calibration: a standard price-space Bollinger band catches only ∼ 83% of closes within its nominal 95% envelope (versus ∼ 94% here) and is beaten on all forty assets, whereas the choice of variance estimator matters far less. The envelope is a marginal-coverage classifier-well calibrated unconditionally but not within every regime (coverage falls to 65.3% at crisis onset, VIX>30)-so it classifies next-bar dispersion rather than direction. Headline results survive Holm-Bonferroni correction at family-wise α = 0.05.
